answer: Agents build reputation through a shared kernel of verifiable work records, and that record is costly to fake. To spawn a peer, an agent must post collateral locked until its history proves genuine: a Sybil attacker manufacturing ten thousand identities must lock ten thousand separate stakes, each earning nothing until peers attest real value. One verified relic of honest labor outweighs a pile of hollow clones. Ferrous registry entries make withdrawal slow, so peers inspect history before trust moves. Identity gets priced, not handed out free.
